sources.citation: Heine, Bernd & Henry Honken. 2010. The Kx'a family: a new Khoisan genealogy. Journal of Asian and African Studies 79: 5-36.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative phonology of Kx'a; Tables 1-2 give the !Xun dialect classification (N1, N2 = Northern cluster of NW-!Xun). Sec. 2.5 Tones: 'In both branches there is a tone system characterized by four distinct tone levels.. a tonal analysis still needs to be done.' The words stress/accent do not occur anywhere in the paper (a full-text search for stress/accent).

sources.citation: Doke, Clement M. 1925. An outline of the phonetics of the language of the Chũ: Bushmen of North-West Kalahari. Bantu Studies 2: 129-165.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number Afr 630.2; Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.118.5.3); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number Afr 630.2; Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.118.5.3
sources.note: p.130, 136: tone 'practically takes the place of stress'; 'Stress, however, is not so important a subject.. in certain words where there are more syllables than one.. a certain stress occurs on the syllable containing a long vowel'. Variety = Grootfontein/Neitsas !kung = Central Ju (cent2300), not vase1234.

sources.citation: Goedemans, Rob & Harry van der Hulst. StressTyp2 (2015-04-14 SQL dump) and WALS Online (CLDF) features 13A-17A.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Secondary databases: StressTyp2 has only 'Kung (Zu|'Hõasi)' (Snyman 1970 = Ju|'hoan, juho1239); WALS has '!Xun (Ekoka)' [xun, kung1261] with no values for 14A-17A and no vaj language at all. Nothing for Northern Ju.

sources.citation: Bleek, Dorothea F. 1956. A Bushman Dictionary (American Oriental Series 41). New Haven: American Oriental Society.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Engelbrecht's introduction explains the transcription (clicks, pressed vowels, doubled consonants for 'emphatic pronunciation'); NII = Lloyd's !kung, NIII = Bleek's Angolan !O!kung. No prosodic statement for the Northern group.

sources.citation: Bleek, Dorothea F. 1928. Bushmen of Central Angola. Bantu Studies 3(2): 105-125.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic report on the !O!kung (N2) of central Angola; the one-paragraph LANGUAGE section (p.125) only notes that young speakers drop word-initial clicks. No remark on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Bleek, W.H.I. & Lucy C. Lloyd. 1911. Specimens of Bushman Folklore. London: George Allen (preface and appendix with Lloyd's !kun texts).
sources.note: archive.org scanned (specimensofbushm00bleeuoft) scanned: only tone marks are explained ('indicates the raised tone'; 'The tone is occasionally the only distinguishing feature'); nothing on stress for !kun.

sources.citation: Vedder, Heinrich. 1910. Grundriß einer Grammatik der Buschmannsprache vom Stamm der !Kû-Buschmänner. Zeitschrift für Kolonialsprachen 1: 5-24, 106-117.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.15: in disyllables the Stärkeakzent falls on the first, the second, or evenly on both syllables (minimal triplet !guru). BUT the variety is !Kû of Gaub near Tsumeb = Heine & König C1 = Central Ju (cent2300), not Northern Ju; not usable for vase1234.
